data.cultural_impact: The name Sharvikaas in Hindu culture is often associated with the goddess of wealth, Lakshmi, who is the embodiment of wealth, fortune, and prosperity. It is believed that invoking the name Sharvikaas brings blessings of abundance, prosperity, and financial success.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sharvikaas carries deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is associated with the goddess Lakshmi, who not only represents material wealth but also spiritual wealth, inner peace, and contentment.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sharvikaas or Sharvaksha was a Yadava king of the Haihaiyas, mentioned in the Mahabharata. The name Sharvikaas carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is an ancient Sanskrit epic that describes the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and Kaurava princes.

historical_references.reference: Sharvikaas, also known as Sharvashira, was a king of the coastal region of Kalinga in the 3rd century BCE. He is known for his military prowess and was a contemporary of Ashoka the Great.
historical_references.context: Ashoka the Great was an emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, known for promoting Buddhism throughout his empire.
